spec.title: PROP-027 — `mcp` packages: the agent-server kind and its delivery

status.comment: MCP-SOVEREIGNTY 2026-07-24; remote HTTP and user-scope package registration extended in 1.0.2

p.status-line: **Status:** IMPLEMENTED — the kind and the manifest laws (§2.1–§2.3) shipped with the plan's Wave 1; the servers themselves (Waves 3–4: `mcp:org.vibevm.ai-native/rust-ai-native-mcp`, `…/typescript-ai-native-mcp`, both live-chained vibe-free); the registration lifecycle (§2.4–§2.5) with Wave 5 (`vibe mcp install/uninstall/status` speak package servers; the pin-server fixture e2e pins the walk). §2.7's composition rows inherit the kind-agnostic feature suites — no feature branches on `kind`, and the mcp e2e exercises code-bearing + binaries + the pin end to end. The 1.0.2 extension admits URL-only Streamable HTTP packages, selected project/user registration, global package inventory, and Qwen Code. Units typed at REQ grain; the code carries the matching `scope!` / `#[spec(implements)]` / `#[verifies]` edges.

p.related: **Related:** [PROP-015](PROP-015-mcp-integration.xml) (the product MCP server + the agent-integration command family this PROP extends), [PROP-025](../vibe-workspace/PROP-025-binary-delivery.xml) (binary delivery for local stdio servers), [PROP-024](../../common/PROP-024-code-bearing-packages.xml) (code-bearing local servers), [`VIBEVM-SPEC.md` §4.1](../../../VIBEVM-SPEC.md) (the kind register, amended under owner sanction 2026-07-07).

facts.motivation-gap: The discipline stacks ship engines, gates, CLIs, and type oracles — everything an agent-facing toolchain needs EXCEPT the transport.
facts.prototype-cycle: The prototype topology served them through vibevm's own MCP (`vibe mcp serve` + the `tcg_*` adapters), which put the whole vibevm product into every consumer's runtime path and closed an operational cycle over vibevm itself (the tool served its own development).
facts.OWNER-RESOLUTION: The owner's resolution (2026-07-07): agent-server delivery is a first-class package concern — a KIND, not a bolt-on surface — and vibe's job there is install-time wiring, never serving.

p.MCP-KIND-DEF: An **`mcp` package** is one whose primary deliverable is one or more Model Context Protocol servers.

facts.KIND-REGISTER: `kind = "mcp"` joins the installable register (VIBEVM-SPEC §4.1); slots materialise under `vibedeps/<group>.<name>/<version>/` like every other kind (the identity slot — PROP-022 §2.1, owner ruling 2026-08-13; the path carried a kind prefix before that ruling).
facts.TABLE-ONLY-IN-KIND: The `[[mcp_server]]` table (§2.2) is **legal only in this kind** — the kind IS the taxonomy, enforced by `Manifest::validate`, not advisory.
facts.KIND-PROMISES-SERVER: An `mcp`-kind manifest that declares NO `[[mcp_server]]` is refused: the kind promises a server.

manifest.title: 2.2 The `[[mcp_server]]` declaration
manifest.fence: [[mcp_server]] name = "rust-ai-native" # agent-visible server name = the family (PROP-028 §2.4) binary = "rust-ai-native-mcp" # must match a [[binary]] in this manifest description = "AI-Native Rust discipline + type oracle over MCP" args = ["--path", "{project_root}"]
[[mcp_server]] name = "fpf" transport = "streamable-http" url = "https://mcp.fpf.tools/mcp" description = "Official FPF MCP service"

facts.SERVER-IS-BINARY: A local stdio server is a [PROP-025](../vibe-workspace/PROP-025-binary-delivery.xml) binary: delivery, build consent, staleness, and slot residence come from that machinery — `binary` resolves to a `[[binary]]` declared in the same manifest. Existing declarations without `transport` remain stdio.
facts.SERVER-REMOTE-HTTP: A remote server declares `transport = "streamable-http"` and an HTTPS `url`. It needs no `[[binary]]` and no build. The URL is passed to the selected agent's native MCP client; vibe does not proxy traffic or enter the serving path.
facts.SERVER-ONE-TRANSPORT: Exactly one of `binary` and `url` is required. A remote server cannot declare local launch `args`; URL userinfo, fragments, control characters, whitespace, and backslashes are refused. A published URL must contain no secret, including in its query. The package records the endpoint address, not an immutable version of the running remote service.
facts.SERVER-NAME: `name` is what an MCP host shows as the tool namespace; names are unique within the package.
facts.ARGS-CLOSED-SET: `args` may carry substitution tokens ONLY from the closed set `{project_root}` (the absolute, verbatim-free root of the consuming project, resolved at registration time); unknown `{…}` tokens are refused at validation.

facts.VENDORING-WHY: Cargo path-deps cannot cross package slots (PROP-024 §2.4), so a local code-bearing mcp package vendors the crates of the toolchain it serves. A remote URL-only package carries no server code.
facts.SKEW-REOPENED: Vendoring re-opens the version skew the in-slot prototype excluded by construction: a server built from engine copy X enriching against a consumer whose gates run engine copy Y.
facts.EXACT-PIN-LAW: The pin closes it: **every `[requires.packages]` entry of an `mcp`-kind package MUST be an exact `=X.Y.Z` requirement** — the resolver holds the served engines and the consumer's gates to ONE version set; no runtime handshake exists or is needed.
facts.PIN-VALIDATION: `Manifest::validate` refuses any other requirement shape (caret, bare, partial `=X.Y`, compound ranges).
facts.PIN-SOURCES: Git-source deps pin by rev inherently; path-source deps are local-dev surfaces outside this law.

p.REG-TODAY: `vibe mcp install` today writes vibevm's own server into agent configs (PROP-015).

p.REG-PACKAGE-DISCOVERY: The no-selector command retains its established walk over installed package servers. An explicit `mcp:<group>/<name>` selector registers only that package, with optional `--server <name>` for one declaration. A missing package or unsupported agent scope fails visibly instead of succeeding with no entry.

facts.REG-REMOTE-URL: A remote declaration is written as the same HTTPS endpoint in each client's native HTTP MCP shape: Claude Code requires `type = http`, Codex a TOML `url`, Qwen Code JSON `httpUrl`, and the other supported clients their own fields. No local process, shim, or vibe proxy is installed.
facts.REG-MANAGED-SIDECAR: Registration records the package identity and exact owned entry in a separate receipt associated with each agent config. An unowned colliding name or an owned entry changed outside vibe is never overwritten or removed. The older JSON `"vibevm": { "managed": [...] }` marker remains readable for existing registrations; no client-specific unknown member is placed inside an MCP server entry.
facts.REG-PROJECT-SCOPE: Package registration supports the agent's actual project and user scopes. `vibe install -g mcp:<group>/<name>` maintains an exact-pinned user inventory under the Vibe settings root and registers the selected package with explicitly chosen user-scope agents. A local stdio server's `{project_root}` still resolves to the selected project's root; a remote URL is independent of the working directory.
facts.REG-GLOBAL-AGENT-SELECTION: Interactive global MCP install and uninstall use checkboxes: arrows move, Space toggles, Enter confirms and Escape cancels. Checked rows use [+], unchecked rows use [ ]. Install initially checks only the first All row; every individual row starts unchecked. Uninstall uses the verified individual defaults defined by REG-GLOBAL-UNINSTALL-DEFAULTS and initially leaves All unchecked. All and an explicit subset are mutually exclusive: checking All clears every individual row, and checking any individual clears All. Unchecking the last individual leaves an empty selection rather than re-enabling All. Confirming All expands to the caller's managed/found set; explicit rows expand only to those selected. Explicit --agent accepts a comma-separated subset or all alone and bypasses the menu. Empty selections refuse before registration mutation with an explicit-agent remedy. Non-interactive install still requires --agent; non-interactive global uninstall and --assume-yes retain removal of all owned registrations.
facts.REG-GLOBAL-UNINSTALL-DEFAULTS: Global MCP uninstall inspects each selected package's receipt and actual native client config read-only before presenting the menu, parsing each config once for a coherent snapshot. All starts unchecked; an individual agent is checked only if at least one current native server entry matches this package's exact owned payload. A receipt alone or a client executable/marker is not installation proof. Missing, changed and pending entries are labelled and are not automatically selected; unreadable configs fail closed with a safe inspection error. Foreign/unowned entries are never auto-selected or adopted for deletion. Owned candidates remain available for explicit cleanup and existing drift refusal still applies, including a changed sibling server in an otherwise partly registered agent. Discovery changes no config, receipt or package state, emits no payload/credential values or parser source snippets, and does not claim running-server health or authorization.
facts.REG-GLOBAL-SELECTIVE-REMOVAL: Global MCP uninstall removes only the selected agents' owned entries. It preserves the exact-pinned package inventory while another agent registration remains and removes the package after its last owned registration is removed. The global uninstall report exposes package_removed separately from registration results. Ownership, drift refusals and restoration on failed package removal continue to apply. Decision: retain a package still referenced by an unselected agent. Why: removing its local binary slot would break that agent's existing configuration. Rejected: remove all registrations despite a specific selection, or delete the package while references remain. Revisit if receipt ownership gains a different explicit reference model.
facts.REG-REFRESH: lifecycle: `vibe mcp install` re-run refreshes paths after a slot move;
facts.REG-STATUS: `vibe mcp status` distinguishes a remote endpoint from a local built/unbuilt artifact. Configuration presence does not assert live connectivity or authorization; an unbuilt local artifact names the `vibe bin build <name>` recipe.
facts.REG-UNINSTALL: `vibe mcp uninstall` can remove the selected package/server registration and its emptied ownership receipt, preserving every unrelated entry.
facts.REG-DIRECTORY-AUTHORITY: Global MCP registration, ownership discovery, refresh and removal share explicitly supplied invocation-owned user directories. Production resolves the native operating-system home/config directories once; tests inject temporary directories without relying on environment overrides of Windows KnownFolders. Tests must never read or modify the developer's real client configuration. The compatibility path API retains its existing native resolution and client-specific path shapes.
facts.REG-USER-PROJECT-MATERIALISATION: The known service user-project used by global MCP install/update materialises packages automatically, with a normal human notice naming the package count, current-user scope and full actual dependency destination. It asks no separate materialisation question and does not mention internal boot artifacts in that notice. The CLI carries this service scope explicitly; a directory name or path resemblance never grants automatic installation. Concrete-project installation retains default-No confirmation and names its full actual destination. Existing explicit yes, unattended and JSON behavior remains. Automatic user-project materialisation does not rewrite invocation flags or silently approve agent/server choices or local MCP binary consent.

consent.title: 2.5 Consent: registration is the same trust act as building

facts.CONSENT-TRUST-ACT: Registering a local server schedules package code execution at agent-session start; building its binary compiles package code. Registering a remote server gives an agent a connection to the declared endpoint; installation and agent selection are the explicit trust act.
facts.CONSENT-GATE-INHERITED: One trust model, two verbs: registration inherits PROP-025's consent gate verbatim — `org.vibevm` local binaries are allow-listed; another group's local binary requires `--assume-yes` (or is refused with a recipe). URL-only packages build no code; they carry no secret or authentication token.
facts.CONSENT-WRITE-SCOPE: Registration writes touch ONLY the target agent's config files and only managed entries; server processes receive the project root as cwd and NO secrets from vibe.

facts.VIBE-FREE-SERVING: A local package server is launched by the agent host directly from its slot and speaks stdio MCP. A remote package server is contacted by the host's HTTP MCP client at the declared URL. Neither uses vibe at runtime.
facts.VIBE-ROLE: `vibe` is required to install and register; local binaries additionally require a build.
facts.VIBE-FREE-ACCEPTANCE: The acceptance form of this requirement: the server's live chain passes with `vibe` absent from `PATH` and no vibevm process running.

composition.title: 2.7 Composition: an mcp package is a full package

p.COMPOSITION-LAW: Every package-role feature applies to `mcp` packages exactly as to the other kinds; no feature branches on `kind`, so each row inherits its feature's own kind-agnostic suite (the mcp-kind e2e adds the code-bearing + binaries + exact-pin composition end to end):

td.ROW-CODE-BEARING-COMPOSITION-RULE: local binary packages are code-bearing; URL-only packages need no code

td.ROW-BINARIES-COMPOSITION-RULE: the stdio variant references `[[binary]]`; a remote URL has no binary to list or build

td.ROW-SKILLS-COMPOSITION-RULE: `[[skill]]` legal; a server may ship its teaching skill

td.ROW-BOOT-SNIPPET-COMPOSITION-RULE: legal but not required; agents learn servers via registration, not boot text

td.ROW-HOOKS-COMPOSITION-RULE: pre/post-install hooks run in the slot as usual

td.ROW-PUBLISH-COMPOSITION-RULE: standard registry publish; the exact-pin law travels in the manifest

facts.REJ-ANY-KIND: **`[[mcp_server]]` as an any-kind surface** (the plan's original draft): rejected by the owner — the taxonomy should say what a package IS; embedded servers would blur the register and hide the vendoring/pinning obligations §2.3 makes explicit.
facts.REJ-CROSS-SLOT: **Cross-slot path-deps or manifest rewriting** instead of vendoring: PROP-025 v2 territory, specified-only; the reproducible-hash model (PROP-024 §2.2) forbids post-materialise rewriting today.
facts.REJ-VIBE-LAUNCHER: **vibe as the server launcher** (`vibe mcp exec <name>` in agent configs): would keep vibe in the runtime path — the exact property this PROP removes.

facts.OPEN-MULTI-SERVER: A package can declare multiple uniquely named MCP servers. Explicit --server selects a comma-separated subset for global install and selected-package MCP registration/removal; a JSON string array preserves exact names containing delimiters. Each named server must exist; empty tokens and unknown names refuse before configuration writes, duplicates coalesce in declaration order. The UI and internal refresh/removal carry exact server identities rather than reinterpreting names as CLI syntax. An attended interactive global install with multiple declarations and no explicit --server shows the same checkbox interface: only All is checked by default, its [+] is mutually exclusive with every explicit server subset, and confirming All selects every declaration. A single declaration is automatic; noninteractive, JSON, unattended and --assume-yes installs without --server retain all declarations. Updates refresh only servers already owned by each agent and remove vanished declarations; they never silently register a previously unselected server.
facts.OPEN-APP-KIND: The `app` kind (anticipated, VIBEVM-SPEC §4.1) — whether it reuses §2.4's managed-entry machinery for desktop-integration surfaces.
facts.OPEN-STABLE-PATHS: Stable artifact paths (PROP-025 v2 shims) would make managed entries survive version bumps without a re-install; deferred with it.
